    85	/-- The products `A_a B_b` of the effects of two projective measurements on a
    86	common space are square-summable to the identity. -/
    87	theorem sum_mul_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_one {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
    88	    [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (A : Measurement α ι) (B : Measurement β ι)
    90	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
    91	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
    92	    ∑ ab : α × β, (A.effect ab.1 * B.effect ab.2)ᴴ * (A.effect ab.1 * B.effect ab.2) =
    93	      1 := by
    94	  have hpt : ∀ (a : α) (b : β),
    95	      (A.effect a * B.effect b)ᴴ * (A.effect a * B.effect b) =
    96	        B.effect b * A.effect a * B.effect b := by
    97	    intro a b
    98	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (hA a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
    99	      (hB b).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _ (A.effect a * B.effect b),
   100	      ← Matrix.mul_assoc (A.effect a) (A.effect a), (hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq,
   101	      ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
   102	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
   103	  calc ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α, (A.effect a * B.effect b)ᴴ * (A.effect a * B.effect b)
   104	      = ∑ b : β, B.effect b * (∑ a : α, A.effect a) * B.effect b := by
   105	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   106	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
   107	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hpt a b
   108	    _ = 1 := by
   109	        simp_rw [A.sum_eq_one, mul_one]
   110	        rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => (hB b).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   111	        exact B.sum_eq_one
   112	
   113	/-- The products `B_b A_a` of the effects of two projective measurements on a
   114	common space, indexed by the pair `(a, b)`, are square-summable to the
   115	identity. -/
   116	theorem sum_mul_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_one' {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   117	    [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (A : Measurement α ι) (B : Measurement β ι)
   119	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
   120	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
   121	    ∑ ab : α × β, (B.effect ab.2 * A.effect ab.1)ᴴ * (B.effect ab.2 * A.effect ab.1) =
   122	      1 := by
   123	  have hpt : ∀ (a : α) (b : β),
   124	      (B.effect b * A.effect a)ᴴ * (B.effect b * A.effect a) =
   125	        A.effect a * B.effect b * A.effect a := by
   126	    intro a b
   127	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (hA a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
   128	      (hB b).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _ (B.effect b * A.effect a),
   129	      ← Matrix.mul_assoc (B.effect b) (B.effect b), (hB b).isIdempotentElem.eq,
   130	      ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
   131	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   132	  calc ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β, (B.effect b * A.effect a)ᴴ * (B.effect b * A.effect a)
   133	      = ∑ a : α, A.effect a * (∑ b : β, B.effect b) * A.effect a := by
   134	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   135	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
   136	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hpt a b
   137	    _ = 1 := by
   138	        simp_rw [B.sum_eq_one, mul_one]
   139	        rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   140	        exact A.sum_eq_one

   148	/-- The three closeness conclusions of `lem:qld-4-10` for a pair of projective
   149	families close to the placed sandwiches: with `η` the closeness of `Q` to `R`
   150	on every placement, `C₁ √ε` the closeness of `R` to the ordered product,
   151	`C₂ √ε` the commutation error, and `C₃ ε` the cross-placement consistency of
   152	the ordered products, the distances from `Q` on one placement to the two
   153	ordered products and to `Q` on the opposite placement are bounded by explicit
   154	combinations.  Paper
   155	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:838-881`. -/
   156	theorem chain_bounds (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   157	    (Q : (side : PlayerSide) → PointPair P →
   158	      Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side))
   159	    (η C₁ C₂ C₃ : ℝ)
   160	    (hQR : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   161	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   162	        S.place p ((Q p.side xz).effect ab))
   163	      (fun xz ab => S.place p ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   164	      S.psiHat ≤ η)
   165	    (h₁ : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   166	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   167	        S.place p ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   168	      (fun xz ab => S.place p
   169	        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   170	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   171	      S.psiHat ≤ C₁ * Real.sqrt ε)
   172	    (h₂ : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   173	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p
   174	        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   175	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   176	      (fun xz ab => S.place p
   177	        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   178	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   179	      S.psiHat ≤ C₂ * Real.sqrt ε)
   180	    (h₃ : ∀ p₁ p₂ : Placement, p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
   181	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   182	        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₁
   183	          ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   184	            (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   185	        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
   186	          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   187	            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   188	        S.psiHat ≤ C₃ * ε)
   189	    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂) :
   190	    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   191	        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   192	          S.place p₁ ((Q p₁.side xz).effect ab))
   193	        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
   194	          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   195	            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   196	        S.psiHat ≤ 2 * η + 4 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 4 * (C₃ * ε) ∧
   197	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   198	        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   199	          S.place p₁ ((Q p₁.side xz).effect ab))
   200	        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
   201	          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   202	            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   203	        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * η + 8 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 8 * (C₃ * ε) +
   204	          2 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) ∧
   205	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   206	        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   207	          S.place p₁ ((Q p₁.side xz).effect ab))
   208	        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂ ((Q p₂.side xz).effect ab))
   209	        S.psiHat ≤ 12 * η + 20 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 16 * (C₃ * ε) +
   210	          4 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) := by
   211	  -- `R_1 ≈ M^X M^Z` on the opposite placement
   212	  have hRXZ := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   213	    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ (h₁ p₁) (h₃ p₁ p₂ hopp)
   214	  -- `Q_1 ≈ M^X M^Z` on the opposite placement
   215	  have hQXZ := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   216	    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ (hQR p₁) hRXZ
   217	  -- `Q_1 ≈ M^Z M^X` on the opposite placement
   218	  have hQZX := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   219	    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ hQXZ (h₂ p₂)
   220	  -- `M^Z M^X ≈ Q_2` on the opposite placement
   221	  have hZXQ : opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   222	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₂
   223	        ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   224	          (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   225	      (fun xz ab => S.place p₂ ((Q p₂.side xz).effect ab))
   226	      S.psiHat ≤ 2 * η + 2 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) := by
   227	    rw [opFamilyDistSq_symm]
   228	    exact opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   229	      _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ (hQR p₂) (h₁ p₂)
   230	  have hQQ := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   231	    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ hQZX hZXQ
   232	  refine ⟨by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩
   233

   236	/-! ## Collapsing the error terms into one power -/
   237	
   238	/-- For `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`, the error terms `ε`, `√ε`, and `(C₀ (ε + √ε))^{1/4}`
   239	with `C₀ ≥ 1` are all bounded by multiples of `ε^{1/8}`. -/
   240	theorem error_terms_le_rpow_eighth {ε C₀ : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1)
   241	    (hC₀ : 1 ≤ C₀) :
   242	    ε ≤ Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) ∧ Real.sqrt ε ≤ Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) ∧
   243	      Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
   244	        2 * C₀ * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
   245	  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hε with h0 | hpos
   246	  · subst h0
   247	    have h8 : Real.rpow (0 : ℝ) (1 / 8 : ℝ) = 0 := Real.zero_rpow (by norm_num)
   248	    have h4 : Real.rpow (C₀ * (0 + Real.sqrt 0)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) = 0 := by
   249	      rw [Real.sqrt_zero, add_zero, mul_zero]
   250	      exact Real.zero_rpow (by norm_num)
   251	    rw [h8, h4, Real.sqrt_zero]
   252	    refine ⟨le_rfl, le_rfl, ?_⟩
   253	    positivity
   254	  · have hsqrt : Real.sqrt ε = Real.rpow ε (1 / 2 : ℝ) := Real.sqrt_eq_rpow ε
   255	    have hε1' : Real.rpow ε 1 = ε := Real.rpow_one ε
   256	    have hmono : ∀ y z : ℝ, z ≤ y → Real.rpow ε y ≤ Real.rpow ε z := fun y z hyz =>
   257	      Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge hpos hε1 hyz
   258	    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   259	    · exact le_of_eq_of_le hε1'.symm (hmono 1 (1 / 8) (by norm_num))
   260	    · rw [hsqrt]
   261	      exact hmono (1 / 2) (1 / 8) (by norm_num)
   262	    · have hsum : ε + Real.sqrt ε ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt ε := by
   263	        have : ε ≤ Real.sqrt ε := by
   264	          rw [hsqrt]
   265	          exact le_of_eq_of_le hε1'.symm (hmono 1 (1 / 2) (by norm_num))
   266	        linarith
   267	      have hC : 0 ≤ 2 * C₀ := by linarith
   268	      calc Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ)
   269	          ≤ Real.rpow (2 * C₀ * Real.sqrt ε) (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   270	            apply Real.rpow_le_rpow (by positivity) _ (by norm_num)
   271	            nlinarith [Real.sqrt_nonneg ε]
   272	        _ = Real.rpow (2 * C₀) (1 / 4 : ℝ) * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
   273	            change (2 * C₀ * Real.sqrt ε) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) =
   274	              (2 * C₀) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) * ε ^ (1 / 8 : ℝ)
   275	            rw [Real.mul_rpow hC (Real.sqrt_nonneg ε), Real.sqrt_eq_rpow,
   276	              ← Real.rpow_mul hε]
   277	            norm_num
   278	        _ ≤ 2 * C₀ * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
   279	            refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (Real.rpow_nonneg hε _)
   280	            calc Real.rpow (2 * C₀) (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ Real.rpow (2 * C₀) 1 :=
   281	                  Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by linarith) (by norm_num)
   282	              _ = 2 * C₀ := Real.rpow_one _

     4	# Approximate commutation of the field-valued expanded point measurements
     5	
     6	The approximate commutation of `lem:qld-comm-cons` is stated for the binary
     7	refinements `M^{(Point,W),u,r}_b` of the expanded point measurements.  The
     8	combined point measurements of `lem:qld-4-10` are built here directly from the
     9	`F_q`-valued measurements `M^{(Point,W),u}_a`, so the commutation estimate is
    10	transferred to them.  The transfer is exact: since

    12	`M^{(Point,Z),z}_b = E_s (-1)^{tr(bs)} Z^s(z)`, the commutator of the two
    13	measurement effects is the Fourier transform, in the outcome pair `(a, b)`,
    14	of the commutators of the expanded observables, and Parseval's identity for
    15	the additive characters of `F_q` turns the sum over `(a, b)` of the squared
    16	norms into the average over `(r, s)` of the squared norms of the observable
    17	commutators.  No factor depending on `q` is lost.

    57	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:qld-4-10`: if the coefficient

    62	    [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    63	    (c : J → I → ℂ) (N : ℝ)
    64	    (horth : ∀ i i', ∑ j, (starRingEnd ℂ) (c j i) * c j i' =
    65	      if i = i' then (N : ℂ) else 0)

    67	    ∑ j, ‖∑ i, c j i • v i‖ ^ 2 = N * ∑ i, ‖v i‖ ^ 2 := by

    72	        inner ℂ (v i) (v i')).re := by
    73	    intro j
    74	    rw [hnorm, sum_inner]
    75	    simp only [inner_sum, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right]
    76	    congr 1
    77	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i' _ => ?_

    82	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    83	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]

    96	          inner ℂ (v i) (v i')).re := by

    52	\section{Key theorem forms}
    53	
    54	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    55	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    56	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    57	correlation estimate
    58	\[
    59	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    60	  \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(
    61	    O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    62	\]
    63	Its Fourier--Naimark argument produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector
    64	$\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying,
    65	with
    66	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    67	\[
    68	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    69	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    70	\]
    71	Moreover,
    72	\[
    73	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    74	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    75	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq2\delta.
    76	\]
    77	Equivalently, if $d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}$ denotes the distance between the
    78	binary projective measurements associated with the two observables, then
    79	\[
    80	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    81	  d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}(L^u,O^u\otimes I_{H'})^2\leq\delta.
    82	\]
    83	The provider prints $\delta$ for the first, operator-distance bound.  Its
    84	calculation instead proves the second, measurement-distance bound, which is
    85	one half of the squared operator distance.  The factor-of-two discrepancy and
    86	a counterexample to the printed operator bound are given in
    87	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}, tracked in
    88	\ghissue{124}.
    89	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    90	observable is invertible.
    91	
    92	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    93	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  If $\delta_{x,z}$ is the mean
    94	squared multiplicative defect on that fiber, the corresponding correlation
    95	error is $\delta_{x,z}/2$.  The corrected theorem therefore gives mean squared
    96	operator distance at most $\delta_{x,z}$, equivalently mean squared binary-
    97	measurement distance at most $\delta_{x,z}/2$.  Since the theorem accepts the
    98	actual nonnegative error on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber error is at
    99	most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still formulate
   100	the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space uniform over
   101	$(x,z)$.
   102	
   103	For the combined-point conclusion, take admissible QPBT parameters
   104	$q=2^t,m,M$ and a projective strategy on $H_A\otimes H_B$ with unit state

   107	 \Psi=\psi_{AB}\otimes\Phi_{A'A''}\otimes\Phi_{B'B''},\qquad
   108	 \Phi=q^{-M/2}\sum_{v\in\mathbb F_q^M}|v,v\rangle.
   109	\]

   111	$H_i^+=H_i\otimes(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes M}$ for player $i$'s existing expanded

   113	\[
   114	 d^2(A,B)=\mathop{\mathbb E}_{x,z}\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb F_q}
   115	   \|(A^{x,z}_{a,b}-B^{x,z}_{a,b})\Psi\|^2.
   116	\]
   117	Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-10}, at lines~689--709 of
   118	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}, asserts
   119	projective measurements $Q_i^{x,z}$ on $H_i^+$ with outcomes in
   120	$\mathbb F_q^2$.  The opposite placement pairs are $(AA',BA'')$ and
   121	$(BB',AB'')$, in either direction.  For each such pair $(p_1,p_2)$ its three
   122	conclusions are
   123	\[
   124	 d^2(Q_{p_1},Q_{p_2}),\quad
   125	 d^2(Q_{p_1},(XZ)_{p_2}),\quad
   126	 d^2(Q_{p_1},(ZX)_{p_2})\ \leq\ \delta_Q(\varepsilon),
   127	\]
   128	where $\delta_Q$ is polynomially small in the paper's convention.  Here
   129	$(XZ)^{x,z}_{a,b}=X_a^xZ_b^z$ and $(ZX)^{x,z}_{a,b}=Z_b^zX_a^x$;
   130	subscripts denote register placement, using the measurement for that player.
   131	The direct construction below gives $\delta_Q(\varepsilon)=K\varepsilon^{1/8}$
   132	for a universal $K$, without another ancillary extension.

   134	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
   135	
   136	Lines~711--725 of
   137	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
   138	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
   139	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
   140	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
   141	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The
   142	quotation also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem
   143	and would unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect, and
   144	it appends the assertion at the identity, which follows from exact linearity as
   145	above.  These three are the differences between the quotation and the cited
   146	statement.
   147	
   148	The factor of two is not one of them.  The provider's equation~(3) proves the
   149	bound $\delta$ for binary-measurement distance; under the operator-distance
   150	convention displayed above this is the bound $2\delta$, and it is the
   151	provider's own Theorem~10 that prints $\delta$ for the operator distance.  The
   152	quotation states its conclusion in the relation $\approx_\delta$, which asserts
   153	only an $O(\delta)$ bound and therefore absorbs the constant factor instead of
   154	reproducing the erroneous one.  The normalization defect and its counterexample
   155	are the provider's and are treated in
   156	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}.

   158	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
   159	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
   160	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
   161	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
   162	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
   163	
   164	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
   165	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
   166	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
   167	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
   168	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
   169	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
   170	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
   171	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
   172	
   173	\section{Direct construction of the combined points}
   174	\label{sec:direct-combined-points}
   175	
   176	The source's three-step plan at line~711 and proof at lines~731--881 first
   177	combine binary refinements, prove approximate linearity in their scalar
   178	indices, and apply quantum linearity.  The following replacement retains the
   179	statement of \path{lem:qld-4-10}, but forms and rounds a sandwich with
   180	field-valued outcomes.  The required commutation estimate is obtained without
   181	a factor depending on the field size.
   182	
   183	\paragraph{Parseval transfer.}
   184	Fix a point pair and a placement, suppressing these indices.  With
   185	$\chi(v)=(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(v)}$, the Fourier formulas at paper
   186	lines~384--418 give
   187	\[
   188	 X_a=q^{-1}\sum_r\chi(ar)\widehat X^r,\qquad
   189	 Z_b=q^{-1}\sum_s\chi(bs)\widehat Z^s.
   190	\]
   191	Write $[A,B]=AB-BA$.  Character orthogonality applied to the vectors
   192	$[\widehat X^r,\widehat Z^s]\Psi$ yields the exact identity
   193	\[
   194	 \sum_{a,b}\|[X_a,Z_b]\Psi\|^2
   195	 =q^{-2}\sum_{r,s}\|[\widehat X^r,\widehat Z^s]\Psi\|^2.
   196	\]
   197	Indeed, the commutator Fourier expansion has coefficient $q^{-2}$; squaring
   198	contributes $q^{-4}$, and orthogonality contributes $q^2$.  The remaining
   199	$q^{-2}$ is precisely uniform averaging.  This is finite-dimensional Parseval
   200	for vector-valued sums, not an estimate of each outcome separately.  The
   201	observable commutation bound underlying \path{lem:qld-comm-cons}, item~2
   202	(paper lines~466--505 and its proof), therefore gives
   203	$\mathbb E_{x,z}\sum_{a,b}\|[X_a,Z_b]\Psi\|^2\leq C_{\rm com}\sqrt\varepsilon$
   204	on each placement.  Equivalently, the binary-refinement commutators are
   205	$(-1)^{c+d}[\widehat X^r,\widehat Z^s]/4$, so passing from their summed
   206	squared norms to the observable bound costs only a factor of four.
   207	
   208	\paragraph{The sandwich and its overlap.}
   209	For each player and point pair set $R_{a,b}=Z_bX_aZ_b$.
   210	Projectivity gives $R_{a,b}=(X_aZ_b)^\dagger(X_aZ_b)\geq0$ and
   211	$\sum_{a,b}R_{a,b}=I$.  Moreover,
   212	$R_{a,b}-Z_bX_a=Z_b[X_a,Z_b]$, so contraction by $Z_b$ shows
   213	$d^2(R,ZX)\leq C_{\rm com}\sqrt\varepsilon$.
   214	
   215	Now fix opposite placements, denoted by subscripts $1,2$, and a point pair.
   216	Every operator on the first placement commutes with every operator on the
   217	second.  Put
   218	\[
   219	 D^X_a=X_{1,a}-X_{2,a},\quad D^Z_b=Z_{1,b}-Z_{2,b},\quad
   220	 W_b=Z_{1,b}Z_{2,b},\quad K^i_{a,b}=[X_{i,a},Z_{i,b}].
   221	\]
   222	For complete projective measurements $P,Q$ on opposite placements and any
   223	vector $w$, expanding the squared differences gives
   224	\[
   225	 \sum_c\langle w,P_cQ_cw\rangle
   226	 =\|w\|^2-\tfrac12\sum_c\|(P_c-Q_c)w\|^2.
   227	\]
   228	Since $R_{1,a,b}R_{2,a,b}=W_b^\dagger X_{1,a}X_{2,a}W_b$, apply this identity
   229	first to $X_1,X_2$ in $W_b\Psi$, and then to $Z_1,Z_2$ in $\Psi$.  The result is
   230	\[
   231	 1-\sum_{a,b}\langle\Psi,R_{1,a,b}R_{2,a,b}\Psi\rangle
   232	 =\tfrac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b\Psi\|^2
   233	   +\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}\|D^X_aW_b\Psi\|^2.
   234	\]
   235	The left side is the off-diagonal consistency mass because both POVMs are
   236	complete.  This exact identity replaces the source's Cauchy--Schwarz chain
   237	\path{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-1} through \path{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-4}
   238	(paper lines~743--778).
   239	
   240	To bound its second term, use the algebraic decomposition
   241	\[
   242	 D^X_aW_b=W_bD^X_a+Z_{2,b}K^1_{a,b}-Z_{1,b}K^2_{a,b}.
   243	\]
   244	The squared norm of a sum of three vectors is at most three times the sum
   245	of their squared norms.  Projection contraction bounds the last two terms,
   246	and $\sum_b\|W_bv\|^2\leq\sum_b\|Z_{2,b}v\|^2=\|v\|^2$ bounds the first
   247	after summing over $b$.  Thus the off-diagonal mass is at most
   248	\[
   249	 \begin{aligned}
   250	 c(x,z):={}&\tfrac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b\Psi\|^2
   251	       +\tfrac32\sum_a\|D^X_a\Psi\|^2\\
   252	   &+\tfrac32\left(\sum_{a,b}\|K^1_{a,b}\Psi\|^2
   253	       +\sum_{a,b}\|K^2_{a,b}\Psi\|^2\right).
   254	 \end{aligned}
   255	\]
   256	Item~1 of \path{lem:qld-comm-cons} bounds each averaged point-consistency
   257	sum by $C_{\rm sc}\varepsilon$.  Together with Parseval this gives
   258	\[
   259	 \mathbb E_{x,z}c(x,z)\leq
   260	 2C_{\rm sc}\varepsilon+3C_{\rm com}\sqrt\varepsilon
   261	 \leq C_0(\varepsilon+\sqrt\varepsilon),
   262	 \qquad C_0=2C_{\rm sc}+3C_{\rm com}.
   263	\]
   264	All constants can be taken at least one and independent of $q,m,M$ and the
   265	strategy dimensions.

   267	\paragraph{Rounding on the original spaces.}

   227	      ‖applyOperatorToState (X₁.effect ab.1 - X₂.effect ab.1)
   228	          (applyOperatorToState (Z₁.effect ab.2 * Z₂.effect ab.2) ψ)‖ ^ 2 ≤
   229	        3 * (‖applyOperatorToState (Z₂.effect ab.2 *
   230	              (X₁.effect ab.1 - X₂.effect ab.1)) ψ‖ ^ 2 +
   231	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   232	            (X₁.effect ab.1 * Z₁.effect ab.2 -
   233	              Z₁.effect ab.2 * X₁.effect ab.1) ψ‖ ^ 2 +
   234	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   235	            (X₂.effect ab.1 * Z₂.effect ab.2 -
   236	              Z₂.effect ab.2 * X₂.effect ab.1) ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
   237	    intro ab
   238	    obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := ab
   239	    rw [← applyOperatorToState_mul, sub_mul_mul_eq_add_commutators _ _ _ _
   240	      (hXZ a b) (hZX a b) (hZZ b)]
   241	    have hlin : applyOperatorToState
   242	        (Z₁.effect b * Z₂.effect b * (X₁.effect a - X₂.effect a) +
   243	          Z₂.effect b * (X₁.effect a * Z₁.effect b - Z₁.effect b * X₁.effect a) -
   244	          Z₁.effect b * (X₂.effect a * Z₂.effect b - Z₂.effect b * X₂.effect a)) ψ =
   245	        applyOperatorToState (Z₁.effect b)
   246	            (applyOperatorToState (Z₂.effect b * (X₁.effect a - X₂.effect a)) ψ) +
   247	          applyOperatorToState (Z₂.effect b) (applyOperatorToState
   248	            (X₁.effect a * Z₁.effect b - Z₁.effect b * X₁.effect a) ψ) -
   249	          applyOperatorToState (Z₁.effect b) (applyOperatorToState
   250	            (X₂.effect a * Z₂.effect b - Z₂.effect b * X₂.effect a) ψ) := by
   251	      rw [← applyOperatorToState_mul, ← applyOperatorToState_mul,
   252	        ← applyOperatorToState_mul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   253	      unfold applyOperatorToState
   254	      simp only [map_add, map_sub, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.sub_apply]
   255	    rw [hlin]
   256	    set u := applyOperatorToState (Z₁.effect b)
   257	      (applyOperatorToState (Z₂.effect b * (X₁.effect a - X₂.effect a)) ψ)
   258	    set v := applyOperatorToState (Z₂.effect b) (applyOperatorToState
   259	      (X₁.effect a * Z₁.effect b - Z₁.effect b * X₁.effect a) ψ)
   260	    set w := applyOperatorToState (Z₁.effect b) (applyOperatorToState
   261	      (X₂.effect a * Z₂.effect b - Z₂.effect b * X₂.effect a) ψ)
   262	    have hu : ‖u‖ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState
   263	        (Z₂.effect b * (X₁.effect a - X₂.effect a)) ψ‖ :=
   264	      norm_applyOperatorToState_proj_effect_le Z₁ hZ₁ b _
   265	    have hv : ‖v‖ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState
   266	        (X₁.effect a * Z₁.effect b - Z₁.effect b * X₁.effect a) ψ‖ :=
   267	      norm_applyOperatorToState_proj_effect_le Z₂ hZ₂ b _
   268	    have hw : ‖w‖ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState
   269	        (X₂.effect a * Z₂.effect b - Z₂.effect b * X₂.effect a) ψ‖ :=
   270	      norm_applyOperatorToState_proj_effect_le Z₁ hZ₁ b _
   271	    have htri : ‖u + v - w‖ ≤ ‖u‖ + ‖v‖ + ‖w‖ :=
   272	      le_trans (norm_sub_le (u + v) w) (add_le_add (norm_add_le u v) (le_refl ‖w‖))
   273	    have hsq : ‖u + v - w‖ ^ 2 ≤ 3 * (‖u‖ ^ 2 + ‖v‖ ^ 2 + ‖w‖ ^ 2) := by
   274	      nlinarith [sq_nonneg (‖u‖ - ‖v‖), sq_nonneg (‖v‖ - ‖w‖),
   275	        sq_nonneg (‖u‖ - ‖w‖), norm_nonneg (u + v - w), norm_nonneg u,
   276	        norm_nonneg v, norm_nonneg w]
   277	    have hu2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) hu 2
   278	    have hv2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) hv 2
   279	    have hw2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) hw 2
   280	    linarith
   281	  -- the contraction sum over `b`
   282	  have hcontr : ∑ ab : α × β, ‖applyOperatorToState (Z₂.effect ab.2 *
   283	      (X₁.effect ab.1 - X₂.effect ab.1)) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   284	      ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState (X₁.effect a - X₂.effect a) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   285	    simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   286	    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
   287	    exact sum_norm_mul_apply_le Z₂.effect (X₁.effect a - X₂.effect a) ψ
   288	      (measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one Z₂)
   289	  have hsum := Finset.sum_le_sum fun ab (_ : ab ∈ Finset.univ) => hpt ab
   290	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib] at hsum
   291	  linarith
   292	
   293	end Abstract

   299	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}

   301	/-- The pointwise bound on the consistency defect of the sandwich POVM between
   302	two placements, as a function of the point pair: one half of the
   303	`Z`-distance plus three halves of the `X`-distance and of the two placed
   304	commutator sums. -/
   305	def sandwichDefectBound (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p₁ p₂ : Placement)
   306	    (xz : PointPair P) : ℝ :=
   307	  (1 / 2) * ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   308	      (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect b) -
   309	        S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect b)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2 +
   310	    (3 / 2) * ((∑ a : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   311	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect a) -
   312	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect a)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) +
   313	      (∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   314	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   315	            (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) -
   316	          S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   317	            (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) +
   318	      ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   319	        (S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   320	            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) -
   321	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   322	            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)
   323	
   324	/-- The pointwise bound is nonnegative. -/
   325	theorem sandwichDefectBound_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p₁ p₂ : Placement)
   326	    (xz : PointPair P) : 0 ≤ S.sandwichDefectBound p₁ p₂ xz := by
   327	  unfold sandwichDefectBound
   328	  positivity
   329	
   330	/-- For a fixed point pair, the off-diagonal mass of the two placed sandwiches
   331	is at most the pointwise bound.  This is the consistency of the sandwich POVM
   332	between opposite placements, display `eq:rw-sc` of the proof of
   333	`lem:qld-4-10`, paper
   334	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:743-790`, in
   335	exact form. -/
   336	theorem sandwich_offDiagonal_le_sandwichDefectBound (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   337	    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂) (xz : PointPair P) :
   338	    (∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P, ∑ ab' : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   339	      if ab = ab' then 0 else stateQForm S.psiHat
   340	        (S.place p₁ ((S.sandwichPoint p₁.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab) *
   341	          S.place p₂ ((S.sandwichPoint p₂.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab'))) ≤
   342	      S.sandwichDefectBound p₁ p₂ xz := by
   343	  have hdefect := point_defect_eq
   344	    (S.placedMeasurement p₁ (S.sandwichPoint p₁.side xz.1 xz.2))
   345	    (S.placedMeasurement p₂ (S.sandwichPoint p₂.side xz.1 xz.2)) S.psiHat
   346	  simp only [placedMeasurement_effect] at hdefect
   347	  rw [hdefect, psiHat_norm]
   348	  have hkey := sandwich_defect_pointwise_le S.psiHat
   349	    (S.placedMeasurement p₁ (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1))
   350	    (S.placedMeasurement p₂ (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1))
   351	    (S.placedMeasurement p₁ (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2))
   352	    (S.placedMeasurement p₂ (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2))
   353	    (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p₁ _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _))
   354	    (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p₂ _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _))
   355	    (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p₁ _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _))
   356	    (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p₂ _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _))
   357	    (fun a b => S.place_comm p₁ p₂ hopp _ _)
   358	    (fun a b => S.place_comm p₁ p₂ hopp _ _)
   359	    (fun b => S.place_comm p₁ p₂ hopp _ _)
   360	  simp only [placedMeasurement_effect, psiHat_norm] at hkey
   361	  unfold sandwichDefectBound
   362	  simp only [sandwichPoint_effect, place_mul]
   363	  simpa only [place_mul] using hkey
   364	
   365	/-- The average over the point pair of the pointwise bound is polynomially
   366	small: at most a universal constant times `ε + √ε`.  The `X`- and
   367	`Z`-distances are the self-consistency of item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, and
   368	the two commutator sums are the field-valued commutation estimate. -/
   369	theorem avg_sandwichDefectBound_le :
   370	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   371	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   372	        (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
   373	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P)) (S.sandwichDefectBound p₁ p₂) ≤
   374	          C * (ε + Real.sqrt ε) := by
   375	  obtain ⟨C₁, hC₁, h₁⟩ := expPoint_self_cons
   376	  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂, h₂⟩ := expPoint_comm
   377	  refine ⟨2 * C₁ + 3 * C₂, by linarith, ?_⟩
   378	  intro P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp
   379	  have hε : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε := by
   380	    have hv := WinImplications.strategy_value_le_one S.toStrategy
   381	    have hw := S.win
   382	    linarith
   383	  have hZ : avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P)) (fun xz =>
   384	      ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   385	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect b) -
   386	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect b)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) ≤
   387	      C₁ * ε := by
   388	    rw [avgOver_uniform_snd (α := Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   389	      (fun z => ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   390	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z z).effect b) -
   391	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z z).effect b)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)]
   392	    exact h₁ P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp .Z
   393	  have hX : avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P)) (fun xz =>
   394	      ∑ a : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   395	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect a) -
   396	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect a)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) ≤
   397	      C₁ * ε := by
   398	    rw [avgOver_uniform_fst (β := Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   399	      (fun x => ∑ a : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   400	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X x).effect a) -
   401	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X x).effect a)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)]
   402	    exact h₁ P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp .X
   403	  have hK₁ := h₂ P ε S p₁
   404	  have hK₂ := h₂ P ε S p₂
   405	  unfold opFamilyDistSq at hK₁ hK₂
   406	  unfold sandwichDefectBound
   407	  rw [avgOver_add, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_add,
   408	    avgOver_add]
   409	  have hs : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_nonneg ε
   410	  nlinarith [hZ, hX, hK₁, hK₂, hs, hε, hC₁, hC₂]
   411	
   412	end ProjectiveSetting

     3	/-!
     4	# The sandwich POVM of the expanded point measurements
     5	
     6	The first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` combines the two expanded point
     7	measurements into the sandwich POVM
     8	`R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^{(Point,Z),z}_b M^{(Point,X),x}_a M^{(Point,Z),z}_b`.  The
     9	source forms it from the binary refinements; here it is formed directly with
    10	outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, which the Parseval transfer of
    11	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean` makes possible.  This file
    12	defines the POVM, proves that it is close to the ordered product
    13	`M^Z_b M^X_a` by the approximate commutation, and records the consistency of
    14	the ordered products across opposite register placements, which follows from
    15	the self-consistency of each factor.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint`: the sandwich POVM.
    20	* `sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le`: closeness of the sandwich to the ordered
    21	  product on every placement, with the error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
    22	* `ordered_cross_dist_le`: the ordered product on one placement is close to
    23	  the reversed ordered product on the opposite placement.
    24	
    25	## References
    26	
    27	Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-748`
    28	(the sandwich and display `eq:qld-r-2`), blueprint
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803-960` (`lem:qld-4-10`); the
    30	route is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.
    31	-/
    32	
    33	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    34	
    35	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    36	
    37	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    38	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    39	
    40	noncomputable section
    41	
    42	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    43	
    44	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    45	
    46	/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
    47	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    48	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    49	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    50	    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    51	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq
    52	
    53	/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
    54	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    55	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    56	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    57	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    58	      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    59	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq
    60	
    61	/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
    62	theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    63	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    64	    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    65	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
    66	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
    67	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
    68	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
    69	    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
    70	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
    71	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
    72	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
    73	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
    74	
    75	/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
    76	theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    77	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    78	    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
    79	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
    80	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
    81	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
    82	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
    83	  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
    84	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    85	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
    86	      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
    87	          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
    88	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
    89	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    90	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    91	    _ = 1 := by
    92	        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,
    93	          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
    94	        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one
    95	
    96	/-- The sandwich POVM `R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` of the two expanded
    97	point measurements, with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`.  This is the POVM of the
    98	first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-736`,
   100	formed directly with field-valued outcomes rather than from the binary
   101	refinements; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`. -/
   102	def sandwichPoint (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   103	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   104	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   105	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   106	    (fun ab => (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   107	      (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   108	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2)
   109	    (fun ab => by
   110	      rw [sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   111	      exact Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   112	        (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _))
   113	    (sum_sandwich_eq_one S side x z)
   114	
   115	/-- The effects of the sandwich POVM. -/
   116	@[simp] theorem sandwichPoint_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   117	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   118	    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
   119	    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab =
   120	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   121	        (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   122	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 := rfl
   123	
   124	/-- The sandwich differs from the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` by
   125	`M^Z_b` times the commutator.  This is the algebra behind display
   126	`eq:qld-r-2`, paper
   127	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`. -/
   128	theorem sandwichPoint_effect_sub_ordered (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   129	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   130	    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
   131	    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab -
   132	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   133	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 =
   134	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   135	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   136	            (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 -
   137	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   138	            (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1) := by
   139	  rw [sandwichPoint_effect, mul_sub, ← Matrix.mul_assoc, ← Matrix.mul_assoc,
   140	    pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
   141	
   142	/-- The sandwich POVM is close to the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` on every
   143	register placement, on average over the point pair, with the error of
   144	`lem:qld-comm-cons`.  This is display `eq:qld-r-2` of the proof of
   145	`lem:qld-4-10`, paper
   146	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`, with
   147	field-valued outcomes. -/
   148	theorem sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le :
   149	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   150	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

(A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement β J)
    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (tensorMeasurement A B) := by
  intro ab
  change IsProj (Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2))
  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
  · calc
      Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) *
          Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) =
        Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1 * A.effect ab.1)
          (B.effect ab.2 * B.effect ab.2) := by
            simpa using (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul (A.effect ab.1) (A.effect ab.1)
              (B.effect ab.2) (B.effect ab.2)).symm
      _ = Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) := by
        rw [(hA ab.1).isIdempotentElem.eq, (hB ab.2).isIdempotentElem.eq]
  · exact (Matrix.IsHermitian.ext fun i j => by
      rcases i with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
      rcases j with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
      simp [Matrix.kronecker, (hA ab.1).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply,
        (hB ab.2).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply]).isSelfAdjoint

/-- The squared effects of a POVM sum to at most the identity. This is the
formalization-only estimate `lem:sandwich-povm-square-sum` used in the
contractions underlying `lem:ld-sandwich`; detailed source argument
`references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:930-946`. -/
theorem measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
    {α I : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (M : Measurement α I) :
    ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1 := by
  calc
    ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ ∑ a : α, M.effect a := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro a _
      rw [measurement_effect_hermitian]
      exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one M a)
    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

/-- Right tensor placement preserves the square-summability bound for POVM effects. -/
private theorem rightPlacedMeasurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    (M : Measurement α J) :
    ∑ a : α, (rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (M.effect a))ᴴ *
        rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (M.effect a) ≤ 1 := by
  calc

/-!
# Typed strategy measurements and point observables

This file fixes a projective, possibly heterogeneous strategy for the Pauli
basis test and extracts the typed measurement families used in the analysis.
Malformed answers are folded into a fixed valid answer, so the extracted
families remain complete measurements. The winning hypothesis bounds their
original wrong-form mass by the rejection probability. `Option` is used only
for the completed line-evaluation classes.

## References

The ambient strategy convention and the observable `W^r(u)` are in
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`,
corresponding to blueprint `def:strategy-observables`. The typed question
and answer forms come from blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
-/

instance localSpaceFintype (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :

/-- Select the strategy measurement before outcome postprocessing on one
player side. This is the heterogeneous interpretation of the shared symbol `M` at
paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-184`. -/
def strategyMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    (question : PauliQuestion P) :
    Measurement (PauliAnswer P) (S.LocalSpace side) := by
  cases side with
  | alice => exact S.toStrategy.A question
  | bob => exact S.toStrategy.B question

`def:pauli-question-distribution`. -/

  embedLd P W fun i =>
    match i with
    | .inl (.inl j) => u j
    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
    | .inr _ => 0

/-! ## The canonical scalar identification -/

/-- Identify the direct extended game's scalar field with the Pauli scalar
field.  Both are selected by `fixedFieldModel`; only their proof argument for
admissibility differs. -/
noncomputable def extendedDirectScalarEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd ≃+* PauliScalar P := by
  have h : P.extendedDirectLd.hq = P.hq := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  cases h
  exact RingEquiv.refl _

/-- Transport an extended direct point into the canonical Pauli scalar field. -/
def directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    Fin (2 * P.m + 2) -> PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (u i)

written as a sum of projectors by applying Fourier
identities. Specifically, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^{m}$, and
$a \in \F_q$, define the projector
\begin{equation} \tau^{W, u}_{a} =
  \tau^{W}_{[ g_{\cdot}(u) = a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits}: h
    \cdot \ind_m(u) = a} \tau^{W}_{h}\;. \label{eq:qld-point-obs-def} \end{equation}
Then we can write $\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_a$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
  \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a
  &= \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \,
    W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r
    \cdot \ind_m(u)) \\
    &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
    \Big) \otimes \Big(
    \sum_{h \in \F_q^n}
    (-1)^{\tr( r( h \cdot \ind_m(u)))} \tau^{W}_{h} \Big) \\
  &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
    \Big) \otimes \Big(
    \sum_{a'' \in \F_q}
    (-1)^{\tr(a'' r)} \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big) \\
  &=	\sum_{a',a'' \in \F_q} \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr((a + a' + a'')r)} \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \\
  &= \sum_{\substack{a',a'' \in \F_q \\ a' + a'' = a}}  \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''}\;,
\end{align*}
where in the second line we have used \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} on the
first tensor factor and \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj} on the second, and in the third line we
have used \Cref{eq:qld-point-obs-def}.
For a fixed $u\in\F_q^m$, $r \in \F_q$ and $b \in \F_2$, define a projection
\begin{equation}
	\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \sum_{a \in \F_q : \tr(ar) = b}
        \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \label{eq:qld-def-mptur}
\end{equation}
which can be equivalently written as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-22}
\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \frac{1}{2} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{W}^r(u) \Big)\;.
\end{equation}

The registers that the operators $\hat{W}^r(u)$,
$\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$, and $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b$ act on
depend on context. For example if $W^r(u)$ is viewed as an operator
acting on register $\alice$, then we will view $\hat{W}^r(u)$ as
acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (with the $\tau^W$ observable
acting on register $\alice'$). We generally indicate via subscripts
which registers the operators act on (for example we will write
$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\alice \alice'}$ or $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\bob
  \alice''}$).



\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
derive a bipartite relation of the form
\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
yield
\begin{align*}
  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
\end{align*}

Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.

	both players measure the same operators. Let $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ be the
	expanded state~\eqref{eq:def-psihat}, let
	\[
		\sigma \colon\;
		\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B},\quad
		\mathsf{A}' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}',\quad
		\mathsf{A}'' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}''\,,
		\qquad\qquad
		\theta \colon\;
		\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B},\quad
		\mathsf{A}' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{A}''\,,
	\]
	be the two permutations of the six registers
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$
	given by these transpositions, and let $U_\sigma$ and $U_\theta$ be the
	corresponding permutation unitaries. Write
	$\Pi = \{\Id,\, U_\sigma,\, U_\theta,\, U_\sigma U_\theta\}$ and let
	\[
		\mathcal{R} = \{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}',\; \mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}'',\;
		\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}',\; \mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''\}
	\]
	be the four register placements of
	Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}. Then:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Every $U \in \Pi$ fixes $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and the induced
		action of $\Pi$ on $\mathcal{R}$ is simply transitive.
		\item Let $P$ and $Q$ be operators on
		$\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$, where $\hilb$ is the common Hilbert
		space of registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$, let
		$\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}', \mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' \in \mathcal{R}$ and
		let $U \in \Pi$. Then
		\[
			\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
			\,=\,
			\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} - (Q)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|\,,
		\]
		the placement notation being that of
		Definition~\ref{def:expanded-observables}. Consequently, for
		families $\{P^x_a\}$ and $\{Q^x_a\}$ indexed by a question $x$ drawn
		from a distribution and an answer $a$, and for every $\delta \ge 0$,
		$(P^x_a)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} \approx_\delta (Q^x_a)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'}$
		holds on $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ if and only if
		$(P^x_a)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} \approx_\delta (Q^x_a)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')}$
		does, with the same $\delta$
		(Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}).
	\end{enumerate}
	In particular, taking $\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}' = \mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$
	and $\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' = \mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$, respectively
	$\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' = \mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, the images under
	$U_\theta$, $U_\sigma$ and $U_\sigma U_\theta$ are exactly the three
	symmetric equivalents of Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents},
	with the same error parameter.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:expanded-state, def:EPR, def:symmetric-game, def:povm-distance}
	Each of $\sigma$ and $\theta$ transposes registers carrying isomorphic
	Hilbert spaces --- $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ both carry $\hilb$,
	and the four ancilla registers are all isomorphic to
	$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$ (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}) --- so the
	permutation unitaries $U_\sigma$ and $U_\theta$ are defined and satisfy
	$U (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} U^\dagger = (P)_{U(\mathsf{C})U(\mathsf{C}')}$
	for every operator $P$ and every placement.

	For item~1, both generators fix $\ket{\hat{\psi}} = (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}$:
	the factor $(\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}$ is invariant under
	$\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}$ by the symmetry hypothesis;
	$\sigma$ exchanges the two ancilla factors, which are identical; and
	$\theta$ leaves $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}$
	untouched and exchanges the two halves of each pair in
	$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}$, under which
	$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is invariant (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). The
	action on $\mathcal{R}$ sends $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ to
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$,
	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ and $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ under $\Id$,
	$U_\sigma$, $U_\theta$ and $U_\sigma U_\theta$ respectively, so it is
	simply transitive on the four placements.

	For item~2, insert $U^\dagger U$ and use $U \ket{\hat{\psi}} = \ket{\hat{\psi}}$
	together with unitary invariance of the norm:
	\[
		\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
		= \bigl\| U \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) U^\dagger \, U \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
		= \bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} - (Q)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|\,.
	\]
	Summing the squares over the answers $a$ and averaging over the
	questions $x$ preserves the identity, so the two sides of the asserted
	equivalence of $\approx_\delta$ relations
	(Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) are equal quantities. The final
	assertion is item~1 applied to the placements listed there.
\end{proof}

/-- A nonnegative one-parameter error function bounded by a positive real power.

**Local fix:** The prefactor and exponent are quantified separately. Paper
chapter 14 explicitly obtains `sqrt ε` at

def IsPolyErr (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C r : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ 0 < r ∧ ∀ x, 0 ≤ x →
    0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ C * Real.rpow x r

/-- A nonnegative two-parameter error function bounded by a sum of positive
real powers.

**Local fix:** The prefactor and the two exponents are quantified separately,
and the bound is imposed on the closed nonnegative quadrant. The shorthand at
`04_preliminaries.tex:22-29` reads `poly` of several arguments as a single
power of their product, which forces the pasting error of `lem:pasting` at
`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525` to tend to zero with the collision
error at every fixed positive consistency error; a two-dimensional strategy
refutes the resulting statement. A sum of separate positive powers vanishes
exactly when both errors vanish, and bounds the terms the imported proof of
Fact 4.35 produces. The correction is documented in

def IsPolyErr₂ (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C r s : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ 0 < r ∧ 0 < s ∧ ∀ x y, 0 ≤ x → 0 ≤ y →
    0 ≤ f x y ∧ f x y ≤ C * (Real.rpow x r + Real.rpow y s)

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty: moderate.}  The Pauli basis analysis combines
  binary refinements of the expanded point measurements, then uses quantum
  linearity to recover field-valued outcomes.  We instead combine the
  field-valued measurements directly.  A finite Parseval identity transfers
  the commutation estimate without a field-size loss, and an exact sandwich
  identity supplies the consistency needed for orthonormalization.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight:} the completed construction comprises
  roughly two thousand lines of supporting formal proofs.
  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split:} approximately \textbf{20\% Mathlib}
  and \textbf{80\% project-local}.  The project-local portion consists of the
  finite Fourier identities, register placements, and state-dependent distance
  estimates.
  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} finite sums, complex inner products,
  matrix adjoints, and real powers, together with the existing projective
  rounding theorem.  No new stability theorem is assumed.
\end{itemize}

This proves the combined-point conclusion on the original expanded local
spaces; it does not discharge the separate common-extension problem for
quantum linearity.\footnote{The construction is in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points.lean} and its supporting modules, reviewed
in \ghpr{424}.  The distinct common-extension problem is documented in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex}.}

\section{Key theorem forms}

Fix admissible Pauli basis parameters, with $q=2^t$ and $M=2^m$, and let a
projective strategy pass the test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
Write $V=(\C^q)^{\ot M}$ for one Pauli register and
$\hat\psi=\psi_{AB}\ot\mathrm{EPR}_{A'A''}\ot\mathrm{EPR}_{B'B''}$
for its normalized expanded state.  For points $x,z\in\F_q^m$, write
$X_a^x=\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a$ and
$Z_b^z=\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b$ for the projective point effects
on either player's space $H\ot V$.  A subscript $p$ places an operator on
one of $AA',BA'',BB',AB''$.  For operator families $F,G$ with outcomes $(a,b)$,
define
\[
 d^2(F,G)=\E_{x,z}\sum_{a,b}
   \bigl\|(F^{x,z}_{a,b}-G^{x,z}_{a,b})\hat\psi\bigr\|^2,
\]
where $x,z$ are uniform.  The combined-point lemma asserts that there are
projective measurements $Q^{x,z}$ on each original space $H\ot V$ such that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d^2(Q_p,Q_{p'})&\leq\delta_Q(\eps),\\
 d^2(Q_p,(XZ)_{p'})&\leq\delta_Q(\eps),\\
 d^2(Q_p,(ZX)_{p'})&\leq\delta_Q(\eps)
 \end{aligned}
 \qquad\text{for every directed opposite pair }(p,p').
\]
Here $(XZ)_{a,b}=X_a^xZ_b^z$, $(ZX)_{a,b}=Z_b^zX_a^x$, and the opposite
pairs are $AA',BA''$ and $BB',AB''$, in both directions.  We prove these
bounds with $\delta_Q(\eps)=K\eps^{1/8}$ for one universal constant $K$.
The hypotheses and the three conclusions are unchanged; the replacement is
in the proof, not in the statement.

\section{The source argument}

The combined-point lemma in the subsection ``Combining the $X$ and $Z$
measurements'' of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts the three conclusions above
with polynomially small error.\footnote{See
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
lines~689--709, label \path{lem:qld-4-10}.}
Its proof first constructs binary-outcome sandwiches, proves consistency by
a Cauchy--Schwarz calculation, and orthonormalizes them.  Approximate
linearity then permits a second construction with outcomes in
$\F_q^2$.\footnote{The binary construction and its consistency argument are
at lines~711--790 of the same source, including \path{eq:qld-r-2} and
\path{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-1} through \path{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-4}.
Lines~825--832 apply \path{thm:linearity} and invoke zero-state ancillas.}

The linearity theorem returns an auxiliary space for each point pair.  To
follow this argument literally, one must realize all those spaces inside
one common ancillary extension and account for the zero-state padding.
That construction is not supplied by the fixed expanded-state setting.
The direct proof below avoids this requirement; it makes no assertion that
the common-extension reduction has been proved.

theorem place_AA'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

    S.place .AA' O =
      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
        (heteroKron O
          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_left S O).symm

theorem place_BA''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))

    S.place .AB'' O =
      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
        (heteroKron O
          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_left S O).symm

# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns

Catalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks
(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to
prove the claimed mathematics. Complements
the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level
blockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the
trick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions
bake in*.

Every pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a
paper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all
cross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.

## Why this matters

Kernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:

- Be marked `\leanok` in the blueprint,
- Have a sorry-free proof body,
- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),

and still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof
obligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel
branch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this
codebase.

## Catalogue

- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)
- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)
- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)
- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)
- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)
- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)

---

## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis

**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own
conclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body
is a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no
mathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle
(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the
catalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by
PR [#491].

### Why it's bad

The theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;
the caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the
caller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the
stack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\leanok` tag
misrepresents the actual state of the proof.

### How to spot it

- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's
  conclusion.
- The proof body is one of:
  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`
  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`
  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`
- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,
  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.
- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).

### Concrete example

Historical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):

```lean
theorem mainInduction
    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)
    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :
    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,
      ConsRel strategy.state ...
        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by
  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩
  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩
  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩
```

Here `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type
`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally
the conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this
specific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed
the same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains
the archetypal example of the anti-pattern.

PR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's
fields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across
individual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse
because the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs
that discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped
existential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name
that suggests the paper result has been proved.

### How to fix it

Prefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses
— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's
conclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content
cannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation
to be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open
under a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as
an extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof
debt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not
the preferred shape for new work.

A signature passes the smell test if:

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.PointConsistency

/-!
# Placement calculus on the expanded state

This module records the algebra of the four register placements used by the
combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
`def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.

## References

The placements are those of `def:symmetric-equivalents`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.
The EPR-exchange invariance is proved directly for the involution
`(A' B'')(A'' B')`, which fixes the strategy registers.  Its use for
`lem:qld-4-10` is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

| .BA'', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .BA'', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .BB', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .BB', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .BB', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .AB'', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .AB'', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
  | .AB'', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h

/-- A complete measurement on a local expanded space, placed on one of the
four register pairs, is a complete measurement on the six-register space. -/
def placedMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {α : Type*}
    [Fintype α] (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
    Measurement α (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (fun a => S.place p (M.effect a))
    (fun a => S.place_nonneg p (M.pos a))
    (by rw [← place_finsetSum, M.sum_eq_one, place_one])

/-- The effects of a placed measurement are the placed effects. -/
@[simp] theorem placedMeasurement_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (p : Placement) {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) (a : α) :
    (S.placedMeasurement p M).effect a = S.place p (M.effect a) := rfl

/-- A placed projective measurement is projective. -/
theorem placedMeasurement_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (p : Placement) {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.placedMeasurement p M) := by
  intro a
